## Solution

We evaluate the infinite product

$$P = \prod_{k=5}^{\infty}\frac{(k-1)(k+1)(k-4)(k+4)}{(k-2)^2(k+2)^2}.$$

### Step 1. Write the partial product

Let

$$P_N = \prod_{k=5}^{N}\frac{(k-1)(k+1)(k-4)(k+4)}{(k-2)^2(k+2)^2}.$$

Separating the four factors in the numerator and the two squared factors in the denominator:

$$P_N = \frac{\displaystyle\prod_{k=5}^{N}(k-1)\;\prod_{k=5}^{N}(k+1)\;\prod_{k=5}^{N}(k-4)\;\prod_{k=5}^{N}(k+4)}{\displaystyle\left(\prod_{k=5}^{N}(k-2)\right)^{\!2}\left(\prod_{k=5}^{N}(k+2)\right)^{\!2}}.$$

### Step 2. Evaluate each product as a ratio of factorials

$$\prod_{k=5}^{N}(k-1)=4\cdot5\cdots(N-1)=\frac{(N-1)!}{3!},\qquad \prod_{k=5}^{N}(k+1)=6\cdot7\cdots(N+1)=\frac{(N+1)!}{5!},$$

$$\prod_{k=5}^{N}(k-4)=1\cdot2\cdots(N-4)=(N-4)!,\qquad \prod_{k=5}^{N}(k+4)=9\cdot10\cdots(N+4)=\frac{(N+4)!}{8!},$$

$$\prod_{k=5}^{N}(k-2)=3\cdot4\cdots(N-2)=\frac{(N-2)!}{2!},\qquad \prod_{k=5}^{N}(k+2)=7\cdot8\cdots(N+2)=\frac{(N+2)!}{6!}.$$

Hence

$$P_N = \frac{(N-1)!\,(N+1)!\,(N-4)!\,(N+4)!\;/\;(3!\cdot 5!\cdot 8!)}{(N-2)!^{\,2}\,(N+2)!^{\,2}\;/\;(2!^{\,2}\cdot 6!^{\,2})}.$$

### Step 3. Reduce the factorial ratio

Using $(N-1)!=(N-2)!\,(N-1)$, $(N+1)!=(N+2)!/(N+2)$, $(N-4)!/(N-2)!=1/[(N-2)(N-3)]$, and $(N+4)!=(N+2)!\,(N+3)(N+4)$:

$$\frac{(N-1)!\,(N+1)!\,(N-4)!\,(N+4)!}{(N-2)!^{\,2}\,(N+2)!^{\,2}}=\frac{(N-1)(N+3)(N+4)}{(N-2)(N-3)(N+2)}.$$

### Step 4. Evaluate the constant

$$C=\frac{2!^{\,2}\cdot 6!^{\,2}}{3!\cdot 5!\cdot 8!}=\frac{4\cdot 720^{\,2}}{6\cdot 120\cdot 40320}=\frac{4\cdot 518400}{29030400}=\frac{2073600}{29030400}=\frac{1}{14}.$$

### Step 5. Take the limit

$$P_N=\frac{1}{14}\cdot\frac{(N-1)(N+3)(N+4)}{(N-2)(N-3)(N+2)}.$$

As $N\to\infty$, the ratio of the two cubic polynomials tends to $1$ (leading terms $N^{3}/N^{3}$). Therefore

$$P=\lim_{N\to\infty}P_N=\frac{1}{14}\cdot 1=\boxed{\dfrac{1}{14}}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
